newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan-US insurance talks start ahead of deadline.
newsitem.headline: Japan-US insurance talks start ahead of deadline.

text.p: Japan and the United States began a last-ditch effort on Saturday to resolve a dispute over the deregulation of Japanese insurance market before a Sunday deadline, officials said.
"I sincerely hope this insurance negotiation will be peacefully settled," Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky when the talks opened.
Mitsuzuka thanked Barshefsky for reading his letter while she was in Singapore to attend the inaugural ministerial conference of the World Trade Organisation. The five-day gathering ended on Friday.
He also noted Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto had written to U.S. President Bill Clinton and received a prompt reply. He did not elaborate on the contents of the letters.

Clinton has described the dispute as the biggest trade problem between the two countries. Washington has declined to say what action it would take should the issue not be resolved, but said they were keeping all options open.
The disagreement centres on U.S. charges that Japan is planning to renege on a 1994 trade agreement on the deregulation of its $400 billion insurance market.

Washington has argued that the agreement calls for Tokyo to deregulate the huge primary life and casualty insurance sector, which is dominated by Japanese companies, before unleashing competition in the tiny specialty insurance market. Foreign insurance groups have a firm foothold in the niche market.
A senior Ministry of Finance official said on Friday it was extremely difficult to tell whether the two countries could resolve their differences before Sunday's self-imposed deadline.
High-ranking Japanese and U.S. officials have been in negotiations to resolve the insurance dispute this week, after ministerial meeting on December 7 and 8 in Tokyo broke off without an agreement.

Japanese negotiators have said Saturday's ministerial meeting was the last opportunity for Mitsuzuka and Barshefsky to meet before the deadline, but hinted the possibility of yet another meeting if agreement cannot be reached on Saturday.
